//: Shared cross-language CSV-cell vectors. The TypeScript escaper (packages/export/src/csv-cell.ts, via csv-cell.parity.test.ts) and the Rust escaper (rust/export/src/csv_cell.rs, via tests/csv_cell_parity.rs) are BOTH pinned to this file, so the two cannot drift unnoticed. Regenerate the ranges with scripts/gen-csv-cell-vectors.mjs; author cases by hand. A case that omits an option gets the LIBRARY default for it, not a value spelled out by the harness -- that is what the DEFAULT OPTIONS cases pin.
invisiblePrefixNote: Code points a spreadsheet importer swallows or renders as spacing, yet which do NOT stop a following =/+/-/@ from being evaluated as a formula. Exactly Unicode general categories Cf + Z (Zs, Zl, Zp). TypeScript spells this /[\p{Cf}\p{Z}]/u; Rust spells it as a const range table. Both suites sweep every code point 0..=0x10FFFF against the ranges below, so an engine/table mismatch fails loudly instead of silently re-opening the bypass.
paddingNote: Code points that count as whitespace PADDING for the opt-in `quoteWhitespacePadded` rule (a padded cell is quoted so an importer cannot trim the padding away). Defined as JavaScript `\s`, which is NOT the same set as Rust `char::is_whitespace` (Unicode White_Space): JS includes U+FEFF and excludes U+0085 NEL, White_Space is the other way round. Spelling it as one table is what stops that asymmetry becoming a silent behaviour split.

cases.name: empty stays empty
plain text is untouched
delimiter forces quoting
interior quote is doubled and wrapped
embedded LF forces quoting
embedded CR forces quoting
a comma is NOT quoted when the delimiter is a semicolon
semicolon delimiter forces quoting
equals is a formula trigger
plus is a formula trigger when the exemption is opted out of
minus is a formula trigger when the exemption is opted out of
at is a formula trigger
leading TAB is a formula trigger
leading CR is a formula trigger and forces quoting
BOM cannot hide a trigger
zero-width space cannot hide a trigger
left-to-right mark cannot hide a trigger
non-breaking space cannot hide a trigger
LINE SEPARATOR (Zl, outside Zs) cannot hide a trigger
PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR (Zp, outside Zs) cannot hide a trigger
ordinary spaces cannot hide a trigger
a run of mixed invisibles cannot hide a trigger
RFC 4180 2.4: leading whitespace on a benign value is preserved
RFC 4180 2.4: trailing whitespace on a benign value is preserved
RFC 4180 2.4: a benign value led by a BOM keeps the BOM
an invisible run with no trigger behind it is left alone
a cell of nothing but invisibles is left alone
numeric exemption opted out: a negative measure is guarded
numeric exemption on: a negative measure stays summable
numeric exemption on: a signed integer stays summable
numeric exemption on: exponent notation stays summable
numeric exemption on: a real trigger is still guarded
numeric exemption on: a number behind an invisible is still guarded
numeric exemption on: a number with a payload glued on is still guarded
numeric exemption on: a lone sign is not a number and stays guarded
numeric exemption never applies to =, @ or TAB
padded quoting off (default): a leading-space cell is left bare
padded quoting on: a leading-space cell is wrapped
padded quoting on: a trailing-space cell is wrapped
padded quoting on: an unpadded cell is still left bare
padded quoting on: a trailing BOM counts as padding (JS \s includes U+FEFF)
padded quoting on: NEL U+0085 is NOT padding (JS \s excludes it, Rust White_Space includes it)
padded quoting on: the apostrophe lands in front, so a guarded cell is no longer front-padded
padded quoting on: a guarded cell with trailing padding is still wrapped
numeric exemption on: a bare decimal point with no integer part
numeric exemption on: a trailing decimal point with no fraction
numeric exemption on: an uppercase exponent
numeric exemption on: a dot-grouped integer, which de-DE displayCell emits for -3000
numeric exemption on: a sign and a lone decimal point carry no digit
numeric exemption on: an exponent marker with no exponent digits
numeric exemption on: an exponent sign with no exponent digits
numeric exemption on: a comma-grouped integer, which en-US displayCell emits for -1000
numeric exemption on: a trailing newline is past the end of the number
numeric exemption on: full-width digits are not ASCII digits
numeric exemption on: Arabic-Indic digits are not ASCII digits
numeric exemption on: a space-grouped integer is not one number
DEFAULT OPTIONS: a negative measure is exempt
DEFAULT OPTIONS: a signed integer is exempt
DEFAULT OPTIONS: a real formula trigger is still guarded
DEFAULT OPTIONS: a number with a payload glued on is still guarded
